faq.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, provided the learner has basic foundational English literacy and functional reading comprehension (approximately CEFR A2 level or higher). Month 1 focuses specifically on core foundations—accurate grammar, essential vocabulary, sound awareness, and confidence building—before progressing to advanced workplace communication. A diagnostic assessment in Week 1 identifies individual starting points, and a structured foundational bridge pathway is provided for learners requiring preliminary support.

faq.question: What minimum English level is recommended?
faq.answer: A functional foundational literacy approximately equivalent to CEFR A2 or higher is recommended. Learners should be able to read simple English sentences and understand basic spoken prompts. The course is engineered to elevate learners systematically from functional foundations to upper-intermediate and advanced professional workplace competence (B1–B2+ operational capability).

faq.question: Is there an initial proficiency test?
faq.answer: Yes. Every student undergoes a mandatory diagnostic evaluation during Week 1 (Module 01: 4 Guided Hours). This diagnostic evaluates 6 core factors: spoken fluency, auditory comprehension, reading extraction, syntax accuracy, vocabulary range, and phonological intelligibility. The results establish an unvarnished baseline and inform the learner's personalized 6-month Individual Development Plan (IDP).

faq.question: What happens if the student needs foundational support?
faq.answer: Learners whose Week 1 diagnostic reveals significant gaps in basic literacy, syntax, or vocabulary receive tailored foundational bridge support. This includes supplementary syntax worksheets, guided pronunciation drills, simplified conversational pairing, and customized weekly milestones within their Individual Development Plan to ensure they keep pace with cohort training.

faq.question: Will students practice speaking in class?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Over 60% of guided training hours are dedicated to active, interactive speaking. Students participate in paired role-plays, impromptu speech drills, simulated boardrooms, client de-escalation exercises, and roundtable debates. There is zero passive lecture-watching; every session requires active spoken participation.

faq.question: Is grammar included?
faq.answer: Yes, functional business grammar is extensively covered, primarily concentrated in Module 02 (8 Guided Hours) and reinforced across all subsequent writing and speaking modules. The curriculum focuses on practical spoken and written syntax—essential tenses, modal diplomacy, subject-verb agreement, prepositions, and eliminating common Indian-English errors—evaluated on communicative clarity rather than rote rule memorization.

faq.question: Is pronunciation taught?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 03 (6 Guided Hours) is dedicated to phonological sound awareness, vowel/consonant clarity, word stress, sentence stress, intonation contours, and speaking cadence (130–150 wpm). Students utilize acoustic feedback tools (ELSA Speak) alongside human instructor reviews to systematically enhance speech clarity.

faq.question: Must students change their natural accent?
faq.answer: No, absolutely not. Nova Skills enforces a strict anti-accent bias policy. The goal of this program is 100% international communicative intelligibility and vocal clarity, NOT foreign accent mimicry or accent erasure. Students are never taught to imitate British, American, or other foreign national accents, and regional Indian-English accents are respected as authentic professional identity.

faq.question: Is business writing covered?
faq.answer: Yes, extensively. Month 3 features a dedicated 10-hour module on Professional Business Writing (Module 09), covering executive emails using the BLUF model (Bottom Line Up Front), scannable document formatting, project status reports, executive summaries, meeting minutes, and complaint resolutions, with ethical human-reviewed AI writing workflows.

faq.question: Will students practice client meetings?
faq.answer: Yes. Modules 06, 10, 11, 14, 16, and 18 provide realistic simulations of client meetings, progress check-ins, remote kickoff calls, scope renegotiations, client complaint de-escalations, and consultative discovery sessions in simulated corporate environments.

faq.question: Are presentations and public speaking included?
faq.answer: Yes. Month 4 provides 18 combined guided hours across Module 12 (Professional Presentations & Business Storytelling, 10h) and Module 13 (Public Speaking & Impromptu Communication, 8h). Students design executive slide decks in PowerPoint/Google Slides, master business storytelling, conquer stage fright through somatic grounding, deliver impromptu speeches, and defend recommendations during live panel Q&A sessions.

faq.question: Is leadership communication included?
faq.answer: Yes. Month 5 covers Leadership Communication, Teamwork & Cross-Cultural Intelligence (Module 17: 8h), as well as Executive Presence (Module 15: 8h) and Conflict Resolution (Module 16: 8h). Students master group facilitation, outcome-based delegation, communicating strategic vision, managing change, and inspiring team trust.

faq.question: What does personality development mean?
faq.answer: In this program, personality development is defined strictly as communication, professionalism, and interpersonal competence. It encompasses self-awareness, emotional self-regulation, assertiveness, nonverbal authority, empathy, punctuality, reliability, accountability, and ethical conduct. It does NOT force students to conform to a single personality type (e.g., forced extroversion) or imitate foreign cultural behaviors.

faq.question: Is AI voice practice included?
faq.answer: Yes. AI voice practice begins in Month 1 and continues throughout the entire program using ChatGPT Voice, ELSA Speak, and Otter.ai as on-demand rehearsal partners. In Month 6 (Module 19: 4h), advanced AI workflows are consolidated, teaching students to prompt AI for adversarial interview sparring and audit speech transcripts while maintaining complete independent speaking competence.

faq.question: Are all AI tools and premium licenses included?
faq.answer: The program utilizes free and standard educational tiers of AI tools (ChatGPT, Google Workspace, Grammarly, Zoom, Loom, Otter.ai). The course fee covers all instructional training, proprietary simulation frameworks, and guided feedback; students are not required to purchase commercial enterprise software licenses beyond standard free accounts.

faq.question: Can sessions be recorded?
faq.answer: Yes, simulated role-plays, presentations, and mock meetings may be recorded for private educational critique, self-review, and portfolio compilation within the student's learning drive.

faq.question: Is recording consent required?
faq.answer: Yes, mandatory. In strict adherence to privacy ethics, all recordings require explicit, informed consent from all participants. Students are provided with consent-aware alternatives (such as audio-only submissions or private 1-on-1 instructor evaluations), and student speech recordings are never published or shared publicly without written authorization.

faq.question: How is progress measured?
faq.answer: Progress is evaluated through a transparent three-milestone architecture: Week 1 Baseline Diagnostic, Week 12 Midpoint Practical Examination, and Week 24 Final Capstone Assessment. Performance is evaluated across 5 weighted domains: Speaking/Pronunciation (25%), Listening/Conversation (20%), Business Writing (20%), Presentations/Persuasion (20%), and Professional Behaviour/Capstone (15%).

faq.question: Are role-specific activities included?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 18 (8 Guided Hours) provides dedicated, domain-specific communication tracks tailored to 6 career disciplines: IT & Web Development, Graphic Design & Creative, Digital Marketing & Sales, Video Editing & Motion, Business & Support Administration, and Freelancers & Entrepreneurs.

faq.question: Do students complete every professional track?
faq.answer: No. Under approved academic policy, each student selects and completes ONE primary track aligned with their specific career aspirations. Other tracks may be explored informally only as time permits, ensuring deep, authentic competence in the student's chosen career role without dilution.

faq.question: How many guided hours and months?
faq.answer: The course consists of exactly 6 Months of structured training and 144 Guided Instructional Hours distributed evenly across 20 modules (exactly 24 guided hours per month).

faq.question: What portfolio will students create?
faq.answer: Students compile ONE integrated Professional Communication Portfolio housing exactly 15 verified evidence categories: baseline diagnostic report, IDP, recorded self-intro, 5 business emails, meeting simulation recording, agenda & MoM packet, spontaneous talk, presentation slide deck & Q&A defense, negotiation role-play, conflict-resolution recording, industry-track simulation, final capstone presentation, timed writing exam, before/after comparative growth analysis, and post-course roadmap.

faq.question: What certificate is awarded?
faq.answer: Graduates who complete all 20 modules, submit the verified 15-category portfolio, and achieve a minimum 70% composite score are awarded the official 'Nova Skills Course Completion Certificate: Business English & Personality Development' with a verifiable digital certificate ID.

faq.question: Does it guarantee a CEFR level?
faq.answer: No. While curriculum benchmarks and diagnostic rubrics are referenced against international CEFR descriptors (A2 to C1 operational tiers) for objective educational tracking, Nova Skills does NOT claim or advertise an externally certified or government-accredited CEFR level. Certificates certify internal course completion and demonstrated competency.
